title: Growing an allocated integer vector
description: You can follow pointer returns through growth and inspect the printing boundary.

steps.description: This example calls the used-element count capacity and the allocated length size. resize updates size and returns the pointer from realloc.
push doubles the allocation when the used count reaches size. You increment that count and store val in the new last position.

steps.question: Does printList visit the final stored index?
steps.answer: No. Its condition i < capacity - 1 stops one position early.

steps.description: main allocates ten integers and pushes values 0 through 29. You save each returned pointer back into vec.
The recording prints push messages through 29 but lists values only through 28. You then free vec and return.
